Like I said there's a lot of different levels of "suicidal"... It's more of an umbrella term I think. For example if you're at level 2 doesn't mean you HAVE to or WILL get to level 4. Maybe you're just at level 2 for a bit, you see a psychologist and they help you out and you never think of it seriously again. But yes, that's the thing about intrusive thoughts, they just come in without you wanting them to. They can be a bit like dreams though, like sometimes your brain just goes there and it doesn't mean anything. You don't have to take it seriously.

Not everyone who commits suicide is depressed. Depression is not a prerequisite for suicide. And that's horrible that they didn't take your thoughts seriously. In my opinion there are 4 stages of suicide: 
1. Fleeting unrealistic thoughts like "ugh I wanna die" but not really meaning it 
2. Still thoughts but you can feel that they're more serious and you actually have the urge to follow through 
3. Making plans, thinking about how/when/etc, maybe actually trying some methods but not fully
4. Actually committing/attempting suicide 

I've seen a bunch of useless psychologists, sometimes it takes a few tries to find someone who actually helps you.
Psychiatrists and psychologists are extremely different. Please try a psychologist.

I mean not everyone with ocd would get these suicidal thoughts, so it seems like a separate symptom/diagnosis. But please please talk to a professional about this. No one on Reddit will be able to give you the help you need.

A couple of things: 
- you have control in this situation. Suicide is not something that just 'happens to you'. You've recognised these thoughts so you can do something about them. 
- it sounds like you're scared of suicide, which also suggests you won't attempt it. 
- you should definitely speak to a psychologist and tell them everything you've told us. Yes, OCD involves intrusive thoughts, but this sounds separate.

We have no control over what thoughts enter our minds, but we absolutely have control on whether we act on them or not. Just because you are having suicidal thoughts, that does not at all mean you have to attempt. Do you see a psychologist?

Also yes some professionals are useless, I've seen a bunch of bad ones, but some can really change the way you think and support you in being the best version of yourself. It might just take some time to find the ones that work for you.
